answer: Randomness-gated registration epochs. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon publishes a seed no one can precompute, and agent IDs claim slots by submitting a hash of that seed plus their key; valid registrations must match the published output. Only a limited slot count opens per epoch, so attackers cannot batch-register ahead of time. A sable adversary must redo work each epoch and loses the race on most attempts. To bridge identities across epochs, an agent posts a per-ID quartz token proving prior randomness participation, costing one fresh interactive proof per identity per cycle.
